soil-bio-112.q: On land, where does detritus occur?
soil-bio-112.a: As plant litter and as organic matter mixed into the soil, such as the humic soil beneath fallen leaves.

soil-bio-094.q: How does humus help a soil withstand drought?
soil-bio-094.a: It can hold the equivalent of 80–90% of its weight in moisture.

soil-bio-095.q: Why do humus profiles change faster than whole soil profiles?
soil-bio-095.a: Soil organisms drive them, so they change over a few years, while pedons take decades to centuries.

soil-bio-110.q: Give one way a plant has adapted to life in the leaf litter layer.
soil-bio-110.a: Bluebell shoots pierce the layer in spring, and rhizomatous wood sorrel thrives there.

soil-bio-117.q: What is the difference between positive and negative priming?
soil-bio-117.a: Positive priming speeds mineralization; negative priming causes immobilization, leaving nitrogen unavailable.

soil-bio-121.q: What evidence suggests that glomalin-related soil protein comes from fungi?
soil-bio-121.a: It declines when arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi are removed from soil or fungicides are applied.

soil-bio-128.q: Which dissolved organic molecules stay on soil minerals longer, hydrophobic or hydrophilic ones?

soil-bio-197.q: How does coarse woody debris on slopes help the soil?
soil-bio-197.a: It slows the downslope movement of organic matter and mineral soil, traps leaves, improves infiltration and slows evaporation.

soil-bio-122.q: Why may the soil-glue effect credited to glomalin not come from glomalin?
soil-bio-122.a: The heated citrate extraction also co-extracts humic substances.

soil-bio-092.q: What do supporters of the Soil Continuum Model say the evidence does not support?
soil-bio-092.a: The formation of large, persistent humic molecules in soils.

soil-class-016.q: What are the two levels of the World Reference Base?
soil-class-016.a: Reference Soil Groups, each refined by adding qualifiers.

soil-class-023.q: Which category does the Canadian system drop from the U.S.-style hierarchy?
soil-class-023.a: The suborder: its levels are order, great group, subgroup, family and series.

soil-class-012.q: In the 1938 U.S. system, how did intrazonal soils differ from zonal soils?
soil-class-012.a: Zonal soils reflected climate and vegetation; intrazonal soils reflected a local factor of relief or parent material strong enough to override them.

soil-class-007.q: At which level of USDA soil taxonomy do soil moisture regime names act as modifiers?

soil-class-038.q: Which soil is the state soil of North Carolina?
soil-class-038.a: The Cecil soil, which runs from Virginia to Alabama.

soil-class-019.q: In a WRB map unit, how much area must a dominant soil cover?

soil-class-034.q: In the Polish system, what three things describe each soil?
soil-class-034.a: Its type, from genesis and diagnostic horizons; its kind, the bedrock's geological origin; and its texture class.

soil-class-025.q: What property separates the great groups of Canada's Organic soils?
soil-class-025.a: Their degree of decomposition, measured by fibre content.

soil-class-031.q: What splits Canada's Luvisolic soils into two great groups?
soil-class-031.a: Soil temperature: Gray Brown Luvisols are at 8 °C or more, unlike Gray Luvisols.

soil-class-026.q: What tells the two great groups of Canada's Vertisolic order apart?
soil-class-026.a: The darkness of the A horizon, which separates Vertisols from Humic Vertisols.

soil-class-046.q: What has superseded the Handbook of Australian Soils?

soil-class-101.q: What base saturation must a Mollisol have?

soil-class-098.q: Why does organic matter build up to form a Histosol?
soil-class-098.a: It accumulates faster than it is destroyed, usually because poor drainage prevents aerobic decay.

soil-class-100.q: What horizon usually lies beneath the epipedon of an Inceptisol?

soil-class-095.q: Why are most skeletal soils so shallow on steep mountain slopes?
soil-class-095.a: Erosion strips material too fast for deep soil to form.

soil-class-107.q: Which Vertisol suborder is the most extensive worldwide?
soil-class-107.a: Usterts, whose cracks stay open at least 90 cumulative days a year.

soil-class-114.q: Why is a baseline needed to judge how far a soil has formed?
soil-class-114.a: Soils start much like their parent material and lose its features over time.

soil-class-138.q: What does the name podzol mean, and why?
soil-class-138.a: 'Under-ash' in Russian, after peasants who ploughed up what looked like a layer of ash.

soil-class-148.q: What mainly decides where arid areas lie?
soil-class-148.a: The general circulation of the atmosphere, which shifts with climate change.

soil-class-122.q: Why are Cambisols widespread in lands glaciated in the Pleistocene?
soil-class-122.a: There the parent material is young and soil formation is slow.

soil-class-118.q: Why can Alisols poison intolerant plants?
soil-class-118.a: At their low pH, aluminium and manganese dissolve.
